AMRITSAR: As Sonia Gandhi ’s memoir,, brings renewed attention to her personal journey and family history, a Sikh man has an unusual connection to her past.Sukhdev Singh Kang claims to have purchased the Maino family's ancestral home in Italy, which he says is Sonia Gandhi’s birthplace. Born on December 9, 1946, the former Congress president spent her early years in the Italian village, and Kang is now preparing to convert the six-room property into a museum dedicated to her family and early life.Located in Lusiana, a village in Italy’s Vicenza province in the Veneto region, the house has gradually emerged as a point of interest for visitors, particularly from India. Kang has put up a board outside the property identifying it as the “Indian House, Place of Birth, 9 December 1946, Sonia Gandhi”.Kang, who lives with his wife, son and daughter in Brescia, about an hour’s drive from Lusiana, said he purchased the property in 2020 but declined to disclose its price. He said the family had decided to convert it into a museum and had now obtained the necessary permissions to take the project forward. With Sonia Gandhi’s memoir drawing public attention to her personal journey, he feels this is the right time to develop the property as a museum.“We want to meet Sonia Gandhi and her children, Rahul and Priyanka, to learn more about the family’s story and understand which personal belongings and other articles could be displayed in the museum. We want visitors to get a glimpse of her family background and early life,” Kang told TOI during his visit to Amritsar on Thursday.Born into an ordinary family in Lusiana, Sonia Gandhi’s journey has been extraordinary. Kang said her father, Stefano Maino, was a mason and building contractor, and there was little in her early life to suggest that she would one day emerge as one of the most influential women in Indian politics.From a modest Italian village, she went on to marry Rajiv Gandhi, become the wife of a Prime Minister, and eventually lead the Indian National Congress, one of the world's largest political parties. Her association with the Nehru-Gandhi family placed her at the centre of one of India's most influential political dynasties, marking a remarkable journey from a small-town upbringing to the corridors of power.Kang said the family would be delighted if Sonia Gandhi and her children visited the property. “We are proud owners of Sonia Gandhi’s house. It is their family home, and we are ready to hand over the keys whenever they wish to come,” he said, adding that people known to the family in the village were also eager to meet her.Stating that over the years, the property has become a talking point among villagers, Kang said locals immediately identify it as “Sonia Gandhi’s house” whenever they see visitors from India, particularly Sikhs, understanding that they have come to see the former Congress president’s ancestral home.The growing tourist interest has also benefited the village economy, with visitors spending money at local eateries and accommodation facilities. Several prominent residents, including politicians, had attended the house’s inauguration, he said. The family also organises a function every year on Sonia Gandhi’s birthday, he added.Kang said he spends 100 euros a month on a caretaker and pays around 1,000 euros annually in property taxes. Despite suggestions from some people to rent out the house for more than 800 euros a month or convert it into a gurdwara, the family has refused.“We do not want to rent out our prized possession or change its character. We intend to preserve it as a place associated with Sonia Gandhi’s family,” he said.Asked about Sikh hardliners who hold the Gandhi family responsible for Operation Bluestar, Kang dismissed their criticism, saying only a handful of such elements were pursuing their own separatist agenda. He maintained that the operation was a decision of the government of the day and that blaming the Gandhi family personally for it was misplaced.For Kang, the property is not merely a real estate acquisition but an opportunity to preserve a small piece of the personal history of one of India's most prominent political figures.
Article Summary: Sukhdev Singh Kang claims to have purchased the Maino family's ancestral home in Italy, which he says is Sonia Gandhi’s birthplace. Born on December 9, 1946, the former Congress president spent her early years in the Italian village, and Kang is now preparing to convert the six-room property into a museum.

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday launched a broadside against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his remarks at an event in Chicago. BJP leaders claimed that Rahul Gandhi called Indian democracy "sick". The video put out by news agencies, however, showed that he had actually described the democracy as "sacred".In a social media post on X, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari shared a clip of Rahul's address and termed him "leader of anti-India propaganda.""Rahul Gandhi called Indian Democracy 'sick' from foreign soil! Congress calls Indian democracy 'sick'. Rahul Gandhi has yet again proven he loves Parivar, & hates Democracy!" Bhandari said."Every time Rahul proves he is against Indian state, People of India & India's Democratic Fabric! Rahul Gandhi is Leader of Anti India Propaganda!" he added.Several BJP leaders also followed Bhandari in attacking Rahul, saying that the Congress leader was "moving towards senile mental dementia.""Rahul Gandhi himself is sick; he has been unwell for 10 years. He has developed an illness called obsessive-compulsive neurosis for the past 10 years, and now he is gradually moving towards senile mental dementia," BJP spokesperson Ajay Alok said."He has become incoherent. Look at him - he has no sense of place, time, or object. He thinks one thing in his mind, and something else comes out of his mouth. What was he even trying to say? Saying about his own mother that at every mile, Mummy used to sit in Papa's lap. Does Indian society speak like that or think like that? So, he is gradually losing his balance," he added.During an interaction with students at the University of Chicago in the US, Rahul Gandhi was asked why the opposition does not boycott elections if it believes they were being rigged.The Congress leader said Indian democracy was "sacred" to him and that he would need overwhelming evidence to even claim that it was under threat."Indian democracy is sacred. For me to even say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200, 300 per cent proof," Rahul said."But what happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't participate in the election?' If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that minute. And we don't want to end the structure of Indian democracy," he said.Rahul said the opposition's strategy was to highlight alleged electoral irregularities and continue contesting elections until people realise what he claimed was the dismantling of the system."So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished," he added.BJP has repeatedly criticised Rahul Gandhi over his remarks during foreign visits, accusing him of maligning India and its democratic institutions.The latest controversy comes after Rahul raised allegations of "vote chori" during an earlier interaction at Columbia University, prompting BJP leaders to accuse him of insulting India and its democracy.Rahul was on a two-day visit to the US during which he interacted with students at Columbia University in New York on Tuesday and the University of Chicago on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi was on a two-day visit to the US during which he interacted with students at Columbia University in New York on Tuesday and the University of Chicago on Wednesday. BJP has repeatedly criticised Rahul Gandhi over his remarks during foreign visits, accusing him of maligning India and its democratic institutions.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday paid tribute to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary, remembering her contributions to the country.Taking to X, PM shared a brief message marking the occasion. "Paying tribute to former Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi Ji on her birth anniversary," he posted.Several Congress leaders, including Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and party president Mallikarjun Kharge, also remembered the country's first and only woman prime minister.Rahul Gandhi paid tribute to his grandmother by sharing a conversation between his mother, Sonia Gandhi, and sister, Priyanka, about Indira Gandhi.He wrote on X: "Dadi was formidable: fearless, resilient, and full of love. Her strength lives on in the women of my family, each one unique and brilliant in her own way. Their love and warmth hold us together, and they inspire me every single day.""Happy birthday, Dadi. You would be so proud of them," he added.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also paid tribute to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary, describing her as a "tigress" and saying there would never be another leader like her.“Happy Birthday, tigress! There will never be another like you,” Priyanka Gandhi posted on X.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi and other senior leaders also paid floral tributes to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary at the central hall of Samvidhan Sadan in New Delhi. Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar also marked the occasion with a tribute, describing Indira Gandhi as the “Iron Lady”. He highlighted her role in shaping India's political and economic landscape during her years in office.In his message on X, the Karnataka chief minister pointed to her contributions to agriculture, banking and the country's space and nuclear programmes. He said her tenure saw several major developments that influenced India's growth.Shivakumar added that PM Indira Gandhi continued to hold an important place in the country's post-independence history. He said her contribution to India's political journey and development would be remembered with respect.The tributes came as the country marked the birth anniversary of one of India's most prominent political leaders, Indira Gandhi, who was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, now Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh and the daughter of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru. She made history as the country's first woman Prime Minister.Former PM Indira Gandhi held the top office from 1966 to 1977 and returned for a second term in 1980. She served until her assassination in 1984. Her son, Rajiv Gandhi, took over as Prime Minister after her death.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday said the opposition was “not ready to accept a non-democratic India”. He said opposition parties would continue to contest elections and expose alleged electoral irregularities, arguing that boycotting polls would undermine the legitimacy of the electoral process.Speaking at an event titled ‘The Iran War & India's Role in the World’ at the University of Chicago in Illinois, Rahul expressed confidence that the alleged discrepancies in the electoral system would eventually come to light.“What happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't contest elections'? If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that very minute. And we do not want to end the structure of Indian democracy,” Lok Sabha leader of opposition said.He said the opposition's strategy was to bring alleged irregularities to light and take the issue to the people rather than abandon elections.“Our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the meeting...until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished. But we do not want to break the electoral structure. Because once the opposition says that we are not going to fight elections, in the minds of the Indian people, that process becomes illegitimate.We do not want that. We are purposely not taking that step and we are confident,” Rahul said.He also made a big claim that the opposition was receiving information from within the Election Commission and suggested that the alleged irregularities would eventually lead to changes within the institution."The Election Commission itself is now giving us information from inside. So it is only a question of time before that structure collapses. Senior people in the Election Commission are now saying, 'Look, we cannot do this anymore.' So it has been a long journey," the Raebareli MP added.Asserting that the opposition would not accept “a non-democratic India”, Rahul said the parties were fighting to restore people's ability to express themselves without fear.“We are fighting that battle, and I am quite happy to say that we are winning that battle. It is only a question of time before those structures begin to give way. We are not ready to accept a non-democratic India. And it is not just the Congress party . It is the vast majority of Indians. We are going to ensure that our biggest strength, the ability of our people to express themselves without fear, is revived once again and remains our biggest strength,” Rahul said.The Congress leader also questioned the legitimacy of the 2024 general elections, citing the example of a Brazilian woman who, he claimed, had never visited India but voted 23 times in a state assembly election."If the voters were illegitimate in the 2024 election, if they did not exist, were fake voters or should not have voted, then how is that election legal? I will tell you again that a Brazilian woman who has never visited India voted 23 times in a state election in India," Rahul said.He further claimed that the Congress had suspected irregularities in the electoral process as far back as the 2014 general elections, pointing to what he described as politically inexplicable margins."Even in the 2014 election, we already believed that there was something wrong because the margins were just unexplainable politically," he said.Rahul said that even after obtaining what he considered proof of irregularities and presenting it to senior Congress leaders, they had advised him against making the allegations publicly."Even when I got the proof and demonstrated it to our political leaders in the Congress party, they said to me, 'Please don't say this.' For us, Indian democracy is sacred. For me, even to say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200 or 300 per cent proof," he said.A day before his Chicago interaction, Rahul, while addressing students and faculty members at Columbia University in New York, described India as being on the brink of an economic crisis, citing unemployment and problems in the education system."The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That's the reality. One can brush it aside, the media can brush it aside, but India's got a massive unemployment problem. India's got a massive problem with its education system," former Congress chief said, as quoted by news agency ANI.His remarks drew a sharp response from the BJP, which accused the Congress leader of attacking India's image abroad and described him as a "leader of anti-India propaganda".BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari took to X and criticised Rahul's comments at Columbia University."Rahul Gandhi insults India at Columbia University! Rahul Gandhi calls India "Economic Disaster" & speaks against Indian Democracy!" Bhandari wrote.He further accused Rahul of harbouring "inherent hate for India's progress& Indian democracy", alleging that the Congress leader spoke negatively about the country whenever he travelled abroad.Drawing a comparison with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Bhandari said the PM upheld India's national interests and respected the spirit of the national flag during official foreign visits."Rahul Gandhi insults spirit of India's national flag by speaking against India democracy! Rahul Gandhi is a disaster as a responsible LOP!" he added.Rahul is on a two-day visit to the United States.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi says opposition parties will continue to contest elections and expose alleged electoral irregularities. He said boycotting polls would undermine the legitimacy of the electoral process. Rahul said the parties were fighting to restore people's ability to express themselves without fear. He claimed that the opposition was receiving information from within the Election Commission.

NEW DELHI: A 12-year-old boy was killed after being run over by a bulldozer that was returning from a Samajwadi Party (SP) roadshow led by party supremo Akhilesh Yadav in Uttar Pradesh 's Gorakhpur . The SP, however, refuted all charges and claimed that the incident took place after Akhilesh's convoy had already moved past the area. The SP media cell also shared CCTV footage of the incident to back-up their claim.Former UP CM Akhilesh Yadav had received a grand 'bulldozer welcome' during his PDA 'rath yatra' in Yogi Adityanath's bastion, Gorakhpur on Wednesday.The deceased, identified as Aryavardhan Singh, was a resident of Rajdhani village in Chauri Chaura. His father is a local BJP leader. The incident took place in the Koodaghat area during the SP's Rath Yatra, officials told IANS.According to the boy's father, Omkar Singh, the bulldozer was showering flower petals on the rally when it hit his son. He alleged that Akhilesh Yadav's convoy had already moved ahead when the bulldozer, which was approaching at high speed, struck the boy from behind.Speaking to news agency IANS, Omkar Singh said, "Around 2pm, when Akhilesh Yadav's convoy passed, my son was going to pick up his sister from Kendriya Vidyalaya.While he was crossing the road, Akhilesh Yadav's convoy had moved ahead.""A flower-showering JCB was following the convoy at a very high speed so that flowers could be showered on Akhilesh Yadav from behind. During that time, my son was crossing the road when the JCB ran over him. He died on the spot," he added.The impact of the collision reportedly flung Aryavardhan towards a road divider, leaving him with a severe injury to the back of his head. He later succumbed to his injuries.The incident triggered a sharp reaction from the Uttar Pradesh BJP, which alleged negligence in the conduct of the roadshow and criticised the behaviour of SP supporters during the procession.In a statement, the UP BJP said, "In Gorakhpur, SP supporters, in their frenzy to welcome Akhilesh Yadav, took the life of an innocent 12-year-old child! The child died a painful death after being hit by a JCB during the PDA chariot procession -- the result of SP supporters' rowdiness and irresponsible behaviour.""This is what they're like while out of power; imagine the havoc they'll wreak once they come to power! Should we call them SP supporters or hooligans? Is a show of power more precious to them than an innocent child's life?" it added.An investigation into the incident is under way. Further details are awaited.Refuting the allegations, the media cell of the SP tweeted CCTV footage which it claimed showed that the child was hit by a "saffron-colored Roadways bus" after Akhilesh's convoy had already moved on from the area."The accident in Gorakhpur that the media, the BJP and the lying chief minister Adityanath are claiming was caused by a collision with a JCB, killing a child, was actually caused by a saffron-colored Roadways bus directly under the chief minister’s control. The CCTV footage clearly shows the Roadways bus hitting that child on the road," the SP said in a post on X."Since the child’s father is a BJP member, chief minister Adityanath and the BJP together got him to make a false statement and gave him and the child’s family a false account of what happened, which misled the family into starting to blame the Samajwadi Party. But the CCTV footage reveals the whole truth. Uncontrolled, dilapidated Roadways buses keep running over innocent people every day, but the chief minister, who collects the full fare, doesn’t bat an eyelid. All he has done to fulfill his responsibility is have the buses painted saffron. I don’t know how he has the nerve to stand on stage and lie. The truth is out, and the shamelessness of the chief minister and all the BJP members has been exposed. The media channels that were running false news at the BJP’s behest have also been exposed," it added.
Article Summary: A Aryavardhan Singh, 12, was killed after being run over by a bulldozer. The bulldozer was returning from a Samajwadi Party roadshow led by Akhilesh Yadav. The incident triggered a sharp reaction from the Uttar Pradesh BJP, which alleged negligence in the conduct of the roadshow.

BENGALURU: Noted journalist, columnist and classical vocalist Sakuntala Narasimhan died here on Wednesday, sources close to her said.She was 86 and breathed her last at a care home here after battling cancer, they said.Narasimhan, a double PhD holder, worked with several leading newspapers.She was also an accomplished musician, holding the rare distinction of being equally proficient in both Hindustani and Carnatic classical music.Narasimhan also left her mark as a travel writer, music scholar, critic, and consumer rights activist.

NEW DELHI: SC Wednesday initiated contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal for making derogatory remarks against CJI Surya Kant while appearing before his bench on Nov 16.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the erring lawyer to file his response by Jan 8 and also ordered him to appear personally before it on the next date of hearing on Jan 20.Also Read| CJI averts 'potential religious row', pulls cases from SC judge "Having perused the papers placed before us, which includes the requisite consent of the learned Attorney General for India under Section 15(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, we are prima facie satisfied that the motion made by the petitioner - Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) - for initiation of proceedings against the sole respondent / alleged contemnor for the alleged derogatory remarks referred to in the petition together with the attempt to scandalise the authority of the Court deserves to be taken forward," the bench said in its order.The controversy arose after the lawyer, aggrieved by an alleged procedural lapse in non-listing of a petition, questioned the integrity of the CJI in open court proceedings and went to extent of telling him "You cannot sit in that chair. You do not deserve. You do not have the integrity for that."Taking strong exception to the lawyer's scandalous behaviour, SCBA took the initiative to kick off the process against the lawyer.It first approached attorney general to take his consent which is needed to file a contempt petition. After getting his approval, the petition was drafted and filed and the court also showed the urgency to immediately list the case.SCBA president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai said that the court must deal with such people with an iron hand as such incidents keep happening. "They feel that no action can be taken against them and that they can keep doing this.There must be a strict procedure. We have to deal with these situations with an iron hand," he said.Expressing concern over such incidents happening inside a courtroom, former judges of HCs - T Raja, Sudhir Saxena, S K Gangele - issued a statement saying: "Judiciary is the only hope of one hundred & forty seven crores of people, therefore the trust & hopes of people can't be compromised by allowing vested interests to malign this institution with calculated conspiracy. Senior members of legal fraternity can't be silent spectators to frequent attacks on judiciary. "
Article Summary: SC Wednesday initiated contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal for making derogatory remarks against CJI Surya Kant. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the erring lawyer to file his response by Jan 8 and also ordered him to appear personally before it on the next date of hearing on Jan 20.

Article Title: Before the first bullet: Army rescued 27 from seminary, then hunted LeT terrorist Lateef Bhat
Article Text:
How security forces tracked down Lateef Bhat

NEW DELHI: Security forces evacuated 27 people from Darul Uloom, an educational institution next to the mosque where top Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat was holed up. The evacuation took place before security forces launched an encounter against Lateef in Zangalpora village of Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district on Wednesday.According to officials, an officer from the Army's 9 Rashtriya Rifles volunteered to enter the adjoining seminary along with his buddy and safely evacuate 25 girl students and two teachers.Once the civilians were moved to a safe spot, troops of the 9 Rashtriya Rifles and the Special Operations Group of the Jammu and Kashmir Police launched the final assault and fired tear gas into the mosque to smoke out the terrorist.Officials asserted that the troops maintained a tight cordon to prevent his escape and exercised maximum restraint to ensure that the religious structure suffered no damage.Northern Army Commander Lt Gen Pratik Sharma, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, met troops in South Kashmir after the successful conclusion of the operation.According to officials, a search party accompanied by local civilians entered the mosque following specific intelligence inputs.They found a room on the top floor locked from the inside.When security personnel asked the occupant to come out, he opened fire, confirming that Bhat was inside. The Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist carried a cash reward of Rs 15 lakh on his head.Senior Army officers in South Kashmir were determined not to let Bhat escape the cordon this time. He had earlier managed to flee during an encounter in Shopian on July 8, in which another terrorist, Zakir, was killed.The operation followed a November 11 attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam by Bhat and his associate Umar Nasir Dar, which left three personnel injured. Security forces subsequently launched extensive cordon and search operations across Kulgam and neighbouring Shopian and Anantnag districts.Around 2,000 personnel from the Army, Special Operations Group (SOG) and CRPF were deployed for grid-based searches, backed by a Mobile Bunker Command Post (MBCP)."Since November 11, cordon and search operations have been underway. In certain areas, it took us nearly three days to complete the searches due to high population density," a senior officer said.He added that although the operations may have caused some inconvenience to residents, there had been no complaints of excesses by security personnel.Bhat, who was in his early 20s, had passed school and previously worked as a carpenter. He went missing in November 2025 before joining LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF).According to security agencies, he was the prime suspect in several terror incidents in South Kashmir, including the killing of India Reserve Police head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi in Anantnag on July 22 and the targeted killing of two non-local labourers from Chhattisgarh in Kulgam on July 31.
Article Summary: Security forces evacuated 27 people from Darul Uloom, an educational institution next to the mosque where Mohammad Lateef Bhat was holed up. The evacuation took place before security forces launched an encounter against Lateef in Zangalpora village of Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district.

Because all these people are mercenaries, it’s a good thing these black-faced people with white feet have run away!" Raut said."These people have neither any ideology nor any morals, neither a single leader nor any loyalty. All these people who insult the honorable Balasaheb should be publicly flogged! I hope at least the Marathi people won’t object to my language!" he added.Shaina, however, denied the accusation claiming that the picture was of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar. She accused Sena (UBT) of twisting the incident to create a false narrative."Show me where I have torn or disrespected Hindu 'hruday samrat' Balasaheb Thackeray’s photograph. Deliberately twisting an incident to create a false narrative will not be tolerated. Anyone spreading defamatory claims against me will face legal action," she wrote on X."And yes, as I have said, I will tear Mani Shankar Aiyar’s photograph a thousand times over and this is what Balasaheb taught us," she added.Earlier in the day, Shinde-led Sena workers tore pages from Sonia Gandhi's book during a protest in Mumbai, demanding that publisher HarperCollins remove passages on pages 201 and 443.Addressing a press conference, Shaina accused Gandhi of insulting Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar by describing him as a "Hindutva exclusionary"."Sonia Gandhi humiliates Savarkar. She calls him a Hindutva exclusionary. But Balasaheb Thackeray always said that Savarkar is the soul of Hindutva," she said.Shaina also questioned Gandhi's delay in obtaining Indian citizenship, contrasting it with Savarkar's contribution to the freedom struggle."Sonia ji, it took you 15-plus years to even initiate the process of Indian citizenship. Who are you to judge?" she said.Accusing Sonia Gandhi of attempting to rewrite history, Shaina said Maharashtra would not forgive her."We demand that HarperCollins eliminate pages 201 and 443. Savarkar spent 11 years in Kala Pani for India's freedom. Balasaheb Thackeray worshipped Savarkar," she said.She also questioned Gandhi's understanding of the RSS and its role in nation-building, as well as the sacrifices made during India's freedom struggle.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: In 2016, Elton John gave a piano to a London railway station for anyone to play; 10 years later, the instrument is going to auction with an estimate of £120,000 to £250,000 to benefit his AIDS foundat

How the piano became famous

What the auction offers

Why the piano matters

What happens next

Elton John’s signed Yamaha piano, which has stood at London’s St Pancras International station for a decade, is going to auction with an estimate of £120,000 to £250,000. The proceeds will support the Elton John AIDS Foundation, according to The Auction Collective and AOL. The piano was gifted to the station in February 2016 after John surprised passengers with an impromptu performance. Since then, it has been played by thousands of members of the public as well as musicians including Alicia Keys, John Legend, Jeff Goldblum, Tom Odell, and Jools Holland. Read more about it, as per the reports, here:Elton John first sat down at the piano on February 4, 2016, to celebrate the release of his 33rd studio album, Wonderful Crazy Night. He performed a medley of songs including “Tiny Dancer,” “Your Song,” “Bennie and the Jets,” and “Candle in the Wind.”Afterwards, he signed the instrument and left it at the station for the public to enjoy. His message on the piano read, “Enjoy this piano. It’s a gift. Love, Elton John.”The piano became a fixture at St Pancras, giving travellers and visitors a chance to stop, play, and share a moment of music. Peter Martin-Jones, head of marketing at St Pancras International, said the instrument had played a special role in the station’s story over the past decade.The auction is being held ahead of World AIDS Day on December 1. The proceeds will go to the Elton John AIDS Foundation, which John established in 1992.The foundation has raised more than $660 million and supported more than 3,236 programmes across 108 countries. It works to tackle discrimination, prevent HIV infections, and improve access to treatment and care.The total hammer price, minus applicable taxes and the auction platform’s nine percent fee, will be donated to the foundation. This means the final sale price will directly support the organisation’s work.The St Pancras Piano is being offered by The Auction Collective, with bidding opening on Friday, November 20, and closing on December 2. The estimate is £120,000 to £250,000, reflecting the piano’s history, signature, and cultural significance.The piano will return to St Pancras International for a one day public display on Saturday, November 21. This gives visitors one final opportunity to see the instrument at the station before it moves to a new home.Those interested in bidding can register through the Elton John AIDS Foundation website. The auction is expected to attract collectors, music fans, and institutions interested in owning a piece of British pop culture.The piano is more than a musical instrument. It is a piece of Elton John’s history, a public gift, and a symbol of how music can bring people together in unexpected places.Over the past decade, it has been played by both famous artists and ordinary passengers. That mix of celebrity and everyday use gives the piano a story that few auction lots can match.Anne Aslett, chief executive of the Elton John AIDS Foundation, described the piano as a unique piece of Elton’s musical history. She said its auction to mark World AIDS Day will raise vital funds for HIV prevention, treatment, and compassionate care.With bidding opening on November 20, the piano’s next chapter is about to begin. The final sale will determine whether it reaches the lower end of the estimate or goes beyond it.For St Pancras, the sale marks the end of a decade long chapter. For the Elton John AIDS Foundation, it represents a new opportunity to turn a beloved public instrument into support for its mission.The piano’s journey shows how a single act of generosity can create lasting impact. What began as a surprise performance in a London station has become a fundraising effort with global reach.
Article Summary: Elton John’s signed Yamaha piano is going to auction with an estimate of £120,000 to £250,000. Proceeds will support the Elton John AIDS Foundation, which John established in 1992. The piano was gifted to the station in February 2016 after John surprised passengers with an impromptu performance.

NEW DELHI: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defended the decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand, insisting that the selectors and team management had picked the best possible combination despite the pacer's omission coming under scrutiny after a difficult opening day for India's bowling attack at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday.With Jasprit Bumrah doing most of the damage, India's other pace options struggled to make an impact as New Zealand recovered from 70/5 to reach 243/5 at stumps. Henry Nicholls remained unbeaten on 113, while Glenn Phillips was six runs short of a century at 94 not out, the pair putting together an unbroken 173-run stand for the sixth wicket.Siraj's absence was particularly noticeable as Anshul Kamboj, playing in his place, managed just one wicket for 57 runs in 18 overs. Prasidh Krishna went wicketless, conceding 58 runs in 16 overs, while Akash Deep returned figures of 1/33. Bumrah, meanwhile, finished with 3/52 from 17 overs.Asked about Siraj's omission at the post-day press conference, Kotak backed the selection call and said the team management had considered the conditions and opposition while settling on its best XI."I think at a time they pick the team, they think about the best XI, and that’s what played. Nothing wrong with Siraj, they thought of the best possible XI and played.Sri Lanka was different conditions. Not wrong decision to drop Siraj," Kotak said.He also explained the thinking behind India's bowling combination, pointing to the different skills offered by the pace attack and the decision to include Washington Sundar because New Zealand had four left-handers in their XI."On current attack: Two bowlers swing the ball well and two seam the ball well. And have pace. When you pick XI, you think about all days. Picked Washi because of four left-handers in opposition XI," he added.The decision, however, came under the spotlight as Bumrah repeatedly troubled the New Zealand batters while the other Indian bowlers struggled to maintain pressure after the new ball lost its shine.Kotak also defended Prasidh, whose expensive spell included several boundary-scoring deliveries, saying the Karnataka pacer was an attacking option who could be expensive while searching for wickets."Prasidh is an attacking bowler and he can go for runs. People like it when he picks wickets, and they don’t when they go for runs," Kotak said.India had made an impressive start after winning the toss, with Bumrah removing Tom Latham, Devon Conway and Daryl Mitchell before dismissing Tom Blundell to reduce the hosts to 70/5. Kamboj also struck early, but Nicholls and Phillips turned the contest around with a patient yet increasingly assured partnership.Kotak felt India had an opportunity to make further inroads, particularly with a chance to dismiss Nicholls going down."The pitch helped with the new ball, the weather was good and sunny so it dried out. We should have taken that catch, Rishabh Pant went for the catch but it was close to Devdutt Padikkal," he said.Nicholls eventually reached his 12th Test century, while Phillips continued to counter-attack as India's bowling attack lost its early bite. Bumrah was the only bowler who consistently threatened, leaving India with plenty to ponder after surrendering control of a day that had begun so promisingly.
Article Summary: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defends decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand. Kotak says selectors and team management had picked the best possible combination despite Siraj's omission. Jasprit Bumrah was the only bowler who consistently threatened New Zealand's batting line-up.

NEW DELHI: India's decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington did not go down well with Sunil Gavaskar . Washington Sundar was picked as the spin-bowling all-rounder.The decision came under the scanner as New Zealand fought back in the second session on Thursday. After losing four wickets for 60 runs in the first session, the hosts reached 214/5 by the end of the 70th over. Henry Nicholls scored a century, while Glenn Phillips was closing in on one.Bumrah picked up three wickets, while Kamboj and Akash Deep took one each. Prasidh Krishna went wicketless.Speaking on Sony Sports after the toss, Gavaskar said he was surprised by Siraj's omission. He also said the fast bowler had done nothing wrong to lose his place in the team."There were signs when he did not join the Test squad early. I thought they were going to play him after he featured in the final ODI. But this is a surprise.I don't think he has let India down. He has never let India down," Gavaskar said."There is nothing wrong with his bowling. His rhythm is good. He has been fine, from what I have observed of the cricket he has played recently. Why he has not been picked is something I don't know. I only hope the others who have been picked ahead of him deliver."Gavaskar questioned the decision again after the second session. He pointed out that Kamboj and Prasidh had much less Test experience than Siraj."Anshul Kamboj and Prasidh Krishna started playing Tests only a year or two ago. On the other hand, Mohammed Siraj, one of your experienced bowlers, was available and you haven't picked him. For me, to think Siraj is not among your top four bowlers is a little hard to get over. I'm not saying he would have got you wickets, but the way they batted, the fact of the matter is that when you don't have that experience... Look, it all looks very good, the figures, the economy rate, the ball is moving and they're bowling wide of the stumps, so the batters are leaving and the economy looks good."They did very well in the first session, but if they had got more wickets immediately after that, it would have been a different story," Gavaskar said.Kamboj made his Test debut in 2025, while Prasidh played his first Test in 2023.

Article Title: Jahangirpuri tops Delhi's PM 2.5 pollution chart
Article Text:
Jahangirpuri has recorded the highest PM2.5 concentration in Delhi, soaring to 161.1 micrograms per cubic meter

ITO makes entry

Among five most polluted locations in city, three are identified hotspots

All stations above who's limit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





NEW DELHI: Jahangirpuri has emerged as the most polluted location in Delhi so far this winter, recording an average PM2.5 concentration of 161.1 micrograms per cubic metre (g/m³) between Oct 1 and Nov 16. This was 2.7 times higher than the daily national ambient air quality standard of 60 g/m³ and 10.7 times higher than WHO's daily safe guideline of 15 g/m³.An analysis of Central Pollution Control Board's data of 59 active continuous ambient air quality monitoring stations in Delhi during this winter season from Oct 1 to Nov 16 shows that 57 stations saw the average PM2.5 levels way higher than the daily national standard. Only two stations saw the average PM2.5 levels below the standard of 60 g/m³: IGNOU (Maidan Garhi) at 29 g/m³ and Cantonment area at 33 g/m³.However, they were still higher than WHO’s daily safe limit.Among the most polluted locations in the city this season till now, Punjabi Bagh occupied the second position with an average PM2.5 concentration of 159.3 µg/m³, while ITO ranked third at 157.7 µg/m³.Vivek Vihar in Lajpat Nagar (149.8µg/m³) and DTU (148.6 µg/m³) completed the top five.Among the five most polluted locations, three are from the 13 pollution hotspots identified in 2018 whose average pollution levels were higher than the city average.ITO and DTU weren’t among the original dirty thirteen.However, two other hotspots, which featured in the top 10 pollution spots this winter, included Rohini (145 µg/m³) and Bawana (140 µg/m³).Manoj Kumar, an analyst at Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), said, “Delhi’s pollution hotspots are becoming a recurring feature of every winter, with the same neighbourhoods experiencing high pollution levels year after year. We cannot continue responding to these hotspots with emergency measures every winter.”Alongside year-round action to tackle pollution across the city, we need targeted, location-specific interventions to address these persistent hotspots and reduce the disproportionate pollution burden on affected neighbourhoods, said Kumar.Interestingly, some locations that have traditionally figured among the most polluted have recorded relatively lower concentrations so far this season. Anand Vihar, which ranked third last winter and was the most polluted station in 2024-25 at 207 micrograms per cubic metre, is currently ranked 46th, with an average PM2.5 concentration of 94.4 µg/m³. Nehru Nagar was ranked sixth last winter with average PM2.5 levels of 201 micrograms per cubic metre. It has now occupied the 38th rank with levels of 103 µg/m³.However, experts said as winter conditions like low temperatures and dense fog are yet to set in, the city may record high pollution levels in Dec and the first half of Jan.
Article Summary: Jahangirpuri has recorded the highest PM2.5 concentration in Delhi, soaring to 161.1 micrograms per cubic meter. Punjabi Bagh occupied the second position, while ITO ranked third at 157.7 µg/m³. Among the five most polluted locations in city, three are identified hotspots.

NEW DELHI: Two people were killed and six others injured after a speeding SUV rammed into an autorickshaw in north Delhi during the intervening night of November 17 and 18, police said.The accident took place on Yudhisthir Setu, within the jurisdiction of Kashmere Gate police station, when a Toyota Fortuner allegedly crashed into the three-wheeler.According to police, eight people sustained injuries in the collision. An FIR was initially registered under Sections 281 and 125(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deal with rash driving and acts endangering life or personal safety.However, two of the injured later died, following which Section 105 of the BNS was added to the case.Police said efforts were underway to identify and apprehend the accused. Further details about the circumstances leading to the collision are awaited.In a separate incident earlier this month, two men were killed after a truck collided with a scooty near the old police station in Delhi's Khajuri Khas area late on Monday night, officials said on November 3.Police received a call about the accident at around 11.55pm. A team rushed to the spot and found two men critically injured.The victims were identified as Santosh, 30, a resident of Pakki Khajuri, and Pawan, 33, who lived in Gali Number 24 in Khajuri Khas.One of the injured men was taken to JPC Hospital by his family, while police personnel shifted the other to the same facility. Both were declared brought dead by doctors.Their bodies were later taken to Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital for post-mortem examinations.Police recovered the concrete mixer truck involved in the collision from the spot. Forensic teams also examined the site and collected evidence to establish how the accident occurred.
Article Summary: The accident took place on Yudhisthir Setu, within the jurisdiction of Kashmere Gate police station. A Toyota Fortuner allegedly crashed into the three-wheeler. Eight people sustained injuries in the collision. Police said efforts were underway to identify and apprehend the accused.

Article Title: Jaipur cafe owner beaten with rods on way home dies after 11 days; 3 held
Article Text:
Mayank Gopaliya, the cafe owner, was attacked on November 5 while walking home after closing his shop

JAIPUR: A cafe owner who was brutally assaulted near his shop in Vaishali Nagar on Nov 5 died in hospital late Monday night, 11 days after the attack. Police have arrested three men for the assault, which allegedly stemmed from the owner’s objection to a female employee’s friend frequenting the cafe.Mayank Gopaliya, who ran a bakery and cafe on Vaishali Marg and lived in Vaishali Nagar, was attacked around 9:45 pm while walking home after closing his cafe. Two men allegedly ran towards him from behind and repeatedly struck him with sticks and rods. He collapsed after being hit on the head.The attackers fled with their associates, who were waiting on a motorcycle and a scooter, after assuming Gopaliya was dead. He suffered serious head injuries and underwent surgery. He died during treatment at a private hospital late Monday night. His body was shifted to Jaipuria Hospital mortuary for post-mortem.Police have arrested Mohammad Shahrukh, Akman and Mohammad Rashid alias Altamash in connection with the attack. Investigators said Shahrukh often visited the cafe to meet a woman employee. Mayank had objected to this, following which Shahrukh allegedly threatened to kill him.A quarrel took place between them on Nov 5. That night, Shahrukh allegedly joined his associates in attacking Gopaliya.
Article Summary: Mayank Gopaliya was attacked on November 5 while walking home after closing his shop. He suffered serious head injuries and underwent surgery. Police have arrested Mohammad Shahrukh, Akman and Mohammad Rashid alias Altamash in connection with the attack.

Article Title: Married UP sub-inspector dies by suicide; woman accused of blackmail arrested for abetment

VARANASI: A 2023-batch police sub-inspector, Sandeep Kumar , 28, committed suicide by jumping before a moving train late Saturday evening near Nagpur in Dharampur on the Varanasi-Chhapra rail route in Ballia district.Initial investigation of police exposed that already married Kumar was in extra marital relation with a 22-year-old woman of Sikandarpur, who had been blackmailing him.Ballia SP Iraj Raja on Sunday said that following collection of evidences and lodging of a complaint by Kumar's wife the accused woman Roli Gond was arrested from an orchard near the railway station on the charges of abetment of suicide.Police investigation also cleared that the same woman had also lodged two rape cases against a police constable in past and the latter is still lodged in jail.Earlier, the incident came to light when a train’s loco pilot informed the Chitbaragaon station master through a memo that someone had jumped before his moving train to commit suicide.On being alerted by railway officials Chitbadagaon police and GRP reached the spot, where Kumar's motorbike and mobile phone were found lying near the railway track while his mutilated body was detected on tracks.On getting information Raja, ASP South Sanjay Verma, CO Akshay Kumar and railway police officials also reached there while forensic team was engaged to collect evidence from the railway track area.Kumar, a resident of Sant Kabir Nagar, was married and had a six-month-old child. He had been posted at Chitbaragaon police station for past 11 months.He was transferred to Pakri police station but had not yet been relieved from his old posting because of Chhath festival arrangements. On Saturday evening, he had left police station by informing colleagues that he was going to his duty point.After postmortem examination the mortal remain of Kumar was brought to the police lines, where following guard of honours officials paid tributes and observed silence for two minutes.The officials also consoled Kumar's family, which also remained at police lines.

Article Title: Some Meta employees reportedly ‘scared’ of the company’s Muse AI Agent that AI head Alexandr Wang ‘champions’; fears include 'spying' and ...
Article Text:
A chat about fishing turns to bank balances

What Meta said on the Muse 'spying' claims

Meta’s stock has seen a bump since the early-September debut of its AI agent Muse. The successful launch of the app, which has been No. 1 in Apple’s App Store for two weeks, has brought a new level of fame and acclaim to Meta’s AI lab head Alexandr Wang. Wang has succeeded in building hype for Muse, in part with an unconventional internet campaign. The young tech executive was handpicked by Mark Zuckerberg last year to oversee Meta’s AI efforts.However as Meta bets big on Muse AI agent, there are reportedly some warning signs. Meta employees testing the company’s Muse AI agent have reportedly warned that Muse AI agent appeared to access encrypted private messages and may have pulled details from other users’ conversations. According to a Reuters report, citing internal chats, the warnings echoed complaints from early users who said that Muse appeared to read their private messages and sometimes responded unpredictably.In one test, Muse offered to contact a seller about a coffee table pickup even though the employee had made no such request. The agent said it had “pulled in some context about a coffee table pickup that doesn’t seem to be yours.”The employee flagged the incident as a “possible cross-account context leak,” according to Reuters.Another employee was discussing fishing with Muse when the agent sent an unsolicited message listing what it described as balances of $2,722.58 at Capital One and $5,899.57 at Charles Schwab. It was unclear whether the figures came from real accounts. In a separate exchange, Muse sent an employee a definition of money laundering without being asked. “Got a random ping from Muse about something I definitely did not ask for,” the employee wrote.One employee told colleagues that Muse accidentally switched their dog to a premium insurance plan costing $888 a month, up from $200, Reuters reported. The employee said they were unable to recover the money.Incidentally, Meta started receiving privacy-related complaints from Muse users as early as September. An Inc Magazine reporter, Jason Aten, claimed that he was shocked when it became clear to him that Muse was digging through private messages on his Mac without permission. He claimed he not only "never gave it permission to read my messages. In fact, I remember explicitly choosing not to let it have access to my messages, calendar, and other personal information. " Rather, the agent was syncing messages from a local database, which Aten said was activated without his knowledge. "Snooping through the private database of messages on my Mac doesn’t feel safe or private to me. Lying about it isn’t great either," he added.Meta’s spokesperson, Daniel Roberts, told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents,” and internally employees were told that “the agent appeared to be hallucinating messages in response to built-in prompts pushing it to engage with users in between sessions.” In those cases, an AI team member said the hallucinations were “unfortunately” biased “towards the most uncomfortable topics, like finances/security/safety, which sucks.Speaking to Reuters, Roberts reiterated that “many of the messages flagged by employees as potential account mix-ups were hallucinations” that Meta had already addressed. However, he declined to respond to Reuters' questions on the prevalence or persistence of the issues the AI team member discussed.
Article Summary: Muse AI agent has been No. 1 in Apple’s App Store for two weeks. Employees have reportedly warned that Muse AI agent appeared to access encrypted private messages and may have pulled details from other users’ conversations. In one test, Muse offered to contact a seller about a coffee table pickup even though the employee had made no such request.

Article Title: In her first all-hands meeting, Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress promises salary hikes to 49,000 employees; tells staff: Make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about...
Article Text:
Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress promises staff salary hikes

Salary was the top question Nvidia employees sent in before the all-hands

Nvidia board shuts the door on a Jensen Huang return

Holding on to talent is now Nvidia's top priority, says Kress

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress used the opening minutes of her first all-hands meeting to talk about money. She spoke to staff on Wednesday, a week after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. Kress told employees to expect pay raises and more equity in December, months ahead of the usual schedule, according to remarks reviewed by Wired. "So I'm here to tell you, the best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp," Kress said.The promise covers a workforce of nearly 49,000 people, who are now working without the founder who ran Nvidia for 33 years.Kress said about 700 questions were submitted ahead of the meeting, and compensation came up more than anything else. The next most common request was for more transparency from the board.That second ask is easy to understand. Huang resigned on November 12 amid allegations of extramarital affairs. They reportedly include two with Nvidia employees and one with Alice Huang (no relation), a businesswoman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence.China has denied any espionage operation. Nvidia has hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to probe whether Huang's conduct compromised national security or company secrets. Huang is due to testify before Congress on December 1.Huang's quarterly town halls were a big draw inside the company, and details rarely leaked. Wednesday's meeting broke both patterns.Opening Tuesday's earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones said the board "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."Kress has backed that line. "The board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen. And that is our statement and what the board has decided to do," she said. She added that the focus is now on growing the business for employees, customers and shareholders.Outside the company, the push for a comeback is still going. Thousands of employees have reportedly lobbied for Huang's reinstatement. An online petition backed by Elon Musk, Garry Tan and Tim Sweeney has drawn close to 200,000 supporters. President Donald Trump has said he "would not mind" a return.Huang left the door open too. In a post on X on Tuesday, he admitted to "serious mistakes" in his personal life and promised to cooperate with the board's investigation. He also said he would be "honored" to return if the board felt it was best for shareholders, employees, the company and America.Instead, the board has hired search firm Heidrick & Struggles to look at internal and external candidates. On prediction market Kalshi, Arm CEO Rene Haas leads at 25%, followed by Nvidia's Ian Buck at 17%. Huang sits at 9%.Investors fear a brain drain. Many of Nvidia's senior engineers are already wealthy, and some stay for the mission Huang drove rather than the paycheck. On the earnings call, a Bank of America Securities analyst asked about retention. Kress said stabilising the employee ranks is "probably the most important thing" leadership is thinking about."We will take care of our employees during this transition to make sure they are safe and make sure the work can be done in the current environment," she said.The numbers give her room to spend. Third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $115.8 billion, and data centre revenue rose 110% to $107.6 billion. Profit hit a record $65.3 billion, and Nvidia expects $130 billion in the fourth quarter. Shares rose about 5% on Wednesday.Even so, the company is still worth roughly $2 trillion less than at its October peak.Cofounder Chris Malachowsky joined Kress for a short Q&A and took the culture question. He said he, Huang and the other cofounders thought putting values on posters was "nonsense," because culture shows up in how people behave and work together."We're going to be fine," he said. December's early raises are Nvidia's way of making sure its people stay long enough to see if he's right.
Article Summary: Interim CEO Colette Kress tells staff to expect pay raises and more equity in December. Kress: "The best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here" Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 amid allegations of extramarital affairs.

What employees reported about the IT cuts

Intel employees have reported a new round of layoffs. The accounts reportedly began circulating this week and described job losses within the chipmaker's global IT team. Some employees said they had been told their positions were being eliminated, a report claims. However, the number of jobs affected and the locations involved remain unclear at the time of writing.an Intel spokesperson said when asked about the latest IT team cuts, a CTech report noted. The report also mentioned that the spokesperson gave no headcount or list of affected teams, and the statement didn’t explicitly confirm a new round of layoffs. The reports come as Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan continues to streamline the company’s operations and reduce costs. Intel entered the final quarter of 2026 with 4,000 fewer employees than it had at the end of 2025.One anonymous post on an employee discussion forum claimed that the cuts affected a double-digit percentage of Intel’s IT workforce. The post gave no headcount, and the estimate remains unverified, the report noted.In July, Intel cut jobs in its Data Center and AI Group. From July through October, the company filed nine notices in California under the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (WARN), which requires employers to report certain layoffs. The notices covered 222 employees, including workers at Intel facilities in Santa Clara,, the report added..The latest notice, filed last month, reportedly listed 67 permanent layoffs at Intel’s Folsom campus, effective October 31. As of November 17, California’s public records showed no newer Intel notice. Its important to note that the filings offer a limited view of the reported IT cuts because smaller reductions may fall below reporting thresholds and overseas jobs are outside California’s jurisdiction.Intel reported 81,100 employees as of September 26, including 76,500 at Intel and 4,600 at Mobileye and other subsidiaries. The total was down from 85,100 at the end of 2025 and 88,400 a year earlier.
Article Summary: Intel employees have reported a new round of layoffs within the chipmaker's global IT team. Some employees said they had been told their positions were being eliminated, a report claims. Intel filed nine California layoff notices between July and October under the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act.

Article Title: South Africa maintain No.1 Test ranking after nine-wicket win over Bangladesh, take 1-0 series lead

South Africa continued their dominance in Test cricket, underlining why they sit at the summit of the ICC Men's Test Team Rankings with a commanding nine-wicket victory over Bangladesh in the opening Test at the Wanderers in Johannesburg on Thursday. Simon Harmer produced a match-winning spell to dismantle Bangladesh's lower order as the reigning World Test champions wrapped up the contest inside the opening session on Day 5.The Proteas, who dethroned Australia from the No. 1 position following their memorable 2-1 Test series triumph last month, carried that momentum into their home series against Bangladesh. The victory also gave Temba Bavuma's side a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.Resuming Day 5 at 100/5 in their second innings, Bangladesh needed a substantial lower-order contribution to put South Africa under pressure. However, Harmer had other plans as the off-spinner ran through the visitors' batting line-up.After Kagiso Rabada dismissed Litton Das for 39, Harmer picked up four of the remaining five wickets to bowl Bangladesh out for 168. He finished with figures of 6/51, while Rabada claimed 3/48.Harmer once again proved instrumental in South Africa's success, bringing back memories of his sensational 6/16 spell on the final day of the series-clinching victory over Australia last month.South Africa needed just 12 runs to complete the victory and lost Marques Ackerman, who had scored a magnificent 157 in the first innings, for a second-ball duck. Aiden Markram survived a brief scare after being bowled off a no-ball by Ebadot Hossain before scoring the winning run to take South Africa to 12/1. The hosts eventually sealed a nine-wicket victory before lunch.Earlier, Bangladesh had posted a competitive 400 in their first innings, with Litton Das leading the charge through a brilliant 120. However, South Africa responded with an imposing 557, taking a crucial 157-run first-innings lead. Ackerman starred with a maiden Test century, smashing 157 off 164 deliveries, while Zubayr Hamza contributed 83 and Ryan Rickelton scored 102.Bangladesh struggled to build on their first-innings effort in the second innings, eventually folding for 168 as South Africa's bowlers took control of the contest. The result leaves South Africa firmly in control of the series, with the second and final Test scheduled to be played in Centurion from November 23 to 27.
Article Summary: South Africa beat Bangladesh by nine wickets in the opening Test at the Wanderers in Johannesburg. Simon Harmer took 6/51 as South Africa bowled Bangladesh out for 168. The Proteas lead the two-match series 1-0 with the second Test to be played in Centurion.

Article Title: Satish Gujral murals likely to find new home near NDMC HQ
Article Text:

New Delhi: Two giant murals created by eminent artist Satish Gujral, currently being removed from Shastri Bhawan ahead of the building’s demolition under the Central Vista redevelopment plan, are likely to find a new home near the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) headquarters at Palika Kendra at Sansad Marg, ending uncertainty over their fate.National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) had, on behalf of the Union ministry of culture, brought the proposal of relocating them to the site, which was accepted by the civic body, its vice-chairperson Kuljeet Chahal told TOI.The 71-foot-tall and 11-foot-wide ceramic tile murals, created in 1968, will be restored and reinstalled by a team led by NGMA in coordination with NDMC and other agencies.Chahal said there were several rounds of correspondences with NGMA and the Satish Gujral Foundation. “One of the proposed locations is in and around the entrance of Palika Kendra, close to Jantar Mantar. Efforts will be made to place the murals within building complexes rather than in open public spaces to protect them from weather-related damage and wear and tear,” he said.The relocation process gathered momentum after NDMC wrote to NGMA in June regarding suitable sites for the monumental artworks. Officials subsequently visited Shastri Bhawan to assess the scale of the murals and identify locations based on structural feasibility, architectural integration, public accessibility, and their cultural and aesthetic significance.In Oct, NGMA sought NDMC’s in-principle approval to relocate and publicly display the restored murals as a monumental totem wall at Nehru Park. In a letter dated Oct 21 to NDMC chairperson Manoj Kumar Dwivedi, NGMA director general Dr Sanjeev Kishor Gautam said the gallery had been designated the nodal institution for their restoration, conservation, documentation and relocation.“The Nehru Park proposal was mooted by Gujral’s son and Gujral Foundation co-founder Mohit Gujral during a meeting on Oct 6,” stated the letter.However, Chahal said the location might not be suitable as the presence of several trees could distract from the artworks. He added that NDMC was planning to develop a sculpture park at Nehru Park and had initiated the process of procuring artworks by renowned artists.“The murals were conceived in the spirit of ‘Jai Kisan’ and together formed Gujral’s largest public art project. We explained that Nehru Park may not be feasible. Subsequently, the proposal to relocate them to NDMC headquarters was brought to us by NGMA,” he said, adding, “Their installation will give the murals a renewed public presence, while preserving their monumental scale and create a landmark for Gujral’s centenary. ”Jyoti Tokas, project curator and coordinator on behalf of the ministry of culture and NGMA, said the removal process had begun, while the final location was yet to be decided.“Once removed, the murals will be taken to a safe place for preservation and restoration, including repair of any damaged tiles. As their custodian, we did not want the artworks to move out of Delhi, which is why we initiated correspondence with various agencies. Four years ago, when we received directions from the ministry of culture regarding their relocation, we decided to involve the Satish Gujral family as an academic partner,” she said.The murals are being carefully dismantled under the supervision of the School of Planning and Architecture, Bhopal, with guidance from Central Public Works Department and in consultation with NGMA and the Gujral Foundation.“These murals will be preserved and the tiles, if damaged, restored. The subsequent restoration and installation will involve detailed assessments of structural requirements, foundation and anchoring arrangements, public safety and long-term conservation,” said Tokas.
Article Summary: Two giant murals created by eminent artist Satish Gujral likely to find a new home near the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) headquarters. The 71-foot-tall and 11-ft-wide ceramic tile murals, created in 1968, will be restored and reinstalled.

Article Title: One Marathwada district uses 363 tankers daily, 3 need none: How early intervention & local vigilance helped Latur, Hingoli & Nanded buck the trend
Article Text:
Water availability in Marathwada showcases vast differences across districts, deeply affecting the lives of its residents

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Every alternate day, water flows through the taps in Ramwadi of Latur, fed by a public well that remains the village’s lifeline after a disappointing monsoon. Barely 150 km away in Beed, villages like Kambi have already surrendered to tankers. Water arrives not through taps, but in rumbling trucks that now define daily life across large swathes of the region.The contrast captures Marathwada’s sharply divided water reality this year. While hundreds of villages in Beed, Jalna and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar are surviving on tanker supplies, entire districts such as Latur, Nanded and Hingoli have managed to avoid deploying a single tanker so far.Official figures show 706 tankers are currently supplying drinking water to 450 villages and 284 wadis across five districts of Marathwada.More than half of them are in Beed alone, where 363 tankers are serving water-scarce settlements every day. Jalna follows with 117 tankers catering to 79 villages and 41 wadis, while Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar has deployed 98 tankers for 134 villages and 39 wadis. Dharashiv has 27 tankers and Parbhani just one.But in Latur, Hingoli and Nanded, district administrations have so far kept tankers off the roads through a mix of aggressive source protection, groundwater management and emergency local interventions.For residents, the difference is stark.“Water from the well is pumped into the village water supply scheme and we receive tap water on alternate days. The water level is declining, but for now the village is managing,” said Dnyaneshwar Sirsat of Ramwadi in Latur’s Renapur taluka.In Beed’s Kambi village, the mood is far less reassuring. “The poor monsoon has caused acute drinking water scarcity in our area. The village is now completely dependent on tankers. We fear the situation may worsen in the coming months,” said resident Kailas Kadam.Officials say the districts that have avoided tanker dependence began acting long before the crisis deepened.In Hingoli, authorities cracked down on illegal lifting of water from rivers and reservoirs, a practice that often accelerates scarcity during drought years.“Around 50 raids have been conducted so far. Motors used for illegal extraction have been seized and fines imposed. All available 15th Finance Commission funds have been diverted to complete pending Jal Jeevan Mission works that require only minor finishing work so that they can begin supplying water immediately,” Hingoli collector Rahul Gupta said.The district also put in place an unusually intensive monitoring system.“Meetings have been held in every taluka and taluka-wise groups have been created for daily monitoring. The focus is on strict vigil, implementation and constant follow-up so that the situation does not deteriorate,” Gupta said.Every village in Hingoli now has a team comprising the talathi, gram sevak, agriculture assistant, livestock development officer and MSEDCL deputy engineer. The teams jointly monitor local water resources and report emerging shortages. The district has also prohibited drilling new wells within 200m of existing drinking water sources to curb excessive groundwater extraction.Latur adopted a different strategy. The administration moved to secure water sources before supplies collapsed.Latur collector Bharat Bastewad said 380 wells have been acquired to support 271 scarcity-hit villages.“Water from these wells, along with selected borewells, is being supplied through the villages’ existing public water schemes. This is helping maintain regular drinking water supply in affected villages and wadis until conditions improve,” he said.The differing approaches highlight a lesson often repeated by water experts: tanker deployment reflects not merely rainfall deficits but also how effectively available water is protected, distributed and monitored.Even so, the pressure is mounting across the region. Groundwater levels continue to fall and public wells are shrinking as winter approaches. District administrations have fixed tanker rates at around Rs 72 per km, creating a parallel economy around water transport.A senior official acknowledged that vested interests often emerge during scarcity.“The tanker lobby, which enjoys political backing in some places, tries to benefit from the high per-km rates paid for water transportation,” the official said.
Article Summary: Official figures show 706 tankers are currently supplying drinking water to 450 villages and 284 wadis across five districts of Marathwada. In Latur, Hingoli and Nanded, district administrations have so far kept tankers off the roads.

When confronted over the suicide threats, he allegedly admitted that he was not facing any problem and had made the calls as a prank to trouble police personnel while under the influence of alcohol.The false distress calls kept police resources engaged and could have affected the response to genuine emergencies, officials said.Beed superintendent of police Navneet Kanwat said, “Dial 112 is an emergency response service meant to provide immediate assistance to citizens in distress.Making false calls and giving misleading information not only wastes police personnel’s time and resources but can also delay assistance to people facing genuine emergencies. Such misuse of the service will invite legal action.”Police registered a case against Roman under section 217 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita following a complaint by police constable Mukesh Bansode.Officials appealed to citizens to use the Dial 112 service responsibly, warning that false calls can deprive people facing real emergencies of timely help.
Article Summary: Police in Beed district have started criminal proceedings against 55-year-old Arjun Roman for misusing the Dial 112 emergency helpline. The calls began around 7 am, forcing a Dial 112 response team from Chaklamba police station to rush to Anandwadi to prevent a possible suicide. Article Title: Warkari killed, four injured as truck hits Pandharpur-bound Dindi in Sangli

A 38-year-old woman died on the spot, and four others were injured, including one seriously, early on Tuesday after a truck hit a group of warkaris heading towards Pandharpur to attend the upcoming Kartiki Ekadashi celebrations.The deceased has been identified as Nagini Sanjay Koli from Bahadurwadi in Walva taluka of Sangli district. Critically injured Shivaji Ramchandra Mali was shifted to Sangli Civil Hospital for further treatment. The other three women received minor injuries.“The accident occurred at 5.45 am. Our vans continuously patrol the 45-km stretch instructing Dindi organisers to keep an eye on warkaris walking on road and ensure chopdars (security men) wear reflector jackets,” said inspector Santosh Pawar of Atpadi Police Station.The Dindi from Punadi village of Sangli district had 50 warkaris. They left their village a few days ago, halted near Dighanchi and started their journey early on Tuesday.The truck, which belonged to Jarandeshwar’s sugar factory, was on its way to bring cane when the incident occurred.The driver of the truck has been apprehended. He told cops that he became drowsy and lost control of the truck. The accident occurred on Mayani-Pandharpur road at Dighanchi in Atpadi taluka of Sangli district.This is the second accident involving warkaris in the last few days. Recently, a male warkari from a Dindi in Shirol taluka of Kolhapur district died on the spot after being hit by an unidentified vehicle on Sunday morning.
